A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RefinedFields despite the revised subtitle. All pages, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original novel-view synthesis results, component ablations, a reduced-data Lego case study, and feature-plane inspections, including Tables 2 and 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains original synthetic and Phototourism results, component ablations, and qualitative analyses in Tables 2–3, Figure 3, and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain alternating K-Planes fitting and refinement using Stable Diffusion, LoRA, and the adapted decoder, with unchanged objectives. The fixed-noise and decoder-training clarifications are consistent with v3's procedure and do not establish algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight synthetic scenes, three Phototourism landmarks, and Lego case study using half the training images. The synthetic benchmark moves from v3 Appendix D, Table 5, to v4's main-text Table 2; it is not new coverage.

E2.justification: V4 Table 3 adds Splatfacto-W and WildGaussians to the Phototourism comparison, substantially broadening comparison to strong Gaussian-splatting methods. The separate timing comparison against NeRF-W, Ha-NeRF, CR-NeRF, and K-Planes is removed. Synthetic benchmark comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 adds LPIPS to the Phototourism evaluation alongside PSNR and SSIM. Reported experimental hardware changes from a V100 to an A100, while documented datasets, splits, resolutions, and training budgets remain unchanged. These reporting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing noPrior and noFinetuning ablations gain LPIPS evidence about perceptual quality. The Lego case study and appendix feature-plane inspections are retained unchanged. V3's comparative training-time analysis is dropped, leaving discussion of RefinedFields' own runtime.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: V4 Table 3 adds LPIPS and Gaussian-splatting results that substantially change the comparative picture: WildGaussians has the highest PSNR on all three landmarks. NeRF-W PSNR changes from 24.17/19.20/18.97 to 21.32/19.17/18.61, and its SSIM entries disappear. Retained RefinedFields and K-Planes PSNR/SSIM values and all synthetic scores are unchanged. The reported runtime changes from 150 hours on V100 to approximately 80 hours on A100, which is not a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same feature aggregation, rendering, projection, LoRA formulation, regularization, and optimization objectives. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or formal results are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: V4 reframes the headline contribution around improving planar representations and reducing their quality gap across synthetic and in-the-wild NVS, whereas v3 foregrounds unconstrained-scene modeling. The central refinement claim, improvement over K-Planes, and introductory first-use claim for in-the-wild scene priors remain.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly acknowledges that recent Gaussian-splatting methods outperform the refined planar representations overall and explains why Phototourism scores at different resolutions are not directly comparable. It also explains why freezing the decoder would invalidate the noFinetuning ablation and drops the earlier interpretation of a runtime advantage over competing methods.

D1.justification: V4 Table 4 newly specifies LoRA rank 4, and Appendix A.2 reports publicly available code rather than a future release and identifies A100 hardware. Conversely, v3's proposal-sampling description and general paragraph distinguishing reproduced from borrowed baseline scores are omitted. Most software versions and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially updates positioning through WildGaussians, Splatfacto-W, PI3D, LN3Diff, CAT3D, and other recent work. It distinguishes WildGaussians' pretrained loss-mask network from a prior acting directly on the scene representation and emphasizes refinement of planar representations. Several older background and impact-related citations are removed.

P1.justification: The subtitle and abstract are rewritten, with substantial revisions to the introduction, related work, evaluations, and conclusion around planar representations. The contribution bullets disappear, synthetic evaluation becomes prominent in the main narrative, the separate training-time subsection is absorbed into evaluations, and the appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the two-column format with a single-column journal layout and rearranges Figure 1. The synthetic results table moves into the main text, the duplicated related-work overview is consolidated, the timing table disappears, and the Phototourism table gains methods and LPIPS columns. The underlying images in Figures 1–12 are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 provides stronger contextual evaluation through modern Gaussian-splatting comparators and LPIPS, while explicitly acknowledging the remaining quality gap in Section 4.3. LoRA-rank disclosure and reported code availability also improve reproducibility information. These benefits outweigh the loss of some baseline-provenance and timing detail, although the unexplained NeRF-W score replacements limit transparency. The overall gain is chiefly better-supported positioning and documentation.
